title: Swift Value vs Reference Types, Fast

scenes.say: When you assign a variable in Swift, is it copied or shared? Let's break down value and reference types.

scenes.label: Structs
scenes.sub: Structs and enums are copied on assignment.
scenes.say: Structs and enums are value types. That means they're copied when you assign or pass them.

scenes.label: Classes
scenes.sub: Classes share one instance in memory.
scenes.say: Classes are reference types. Assigning a class just points to the same object in memory.
Here's a struct called Point. If you copy it and change the copy, the original stays the same. That's value semantics in action.
Value types help you avoid accidental bugs and are thread-safe. Reference types can lead to side effects if you’re not careful.

scenes.question: Are structs always better than classes?
scenes.right: No. Use structs for models, but classes for shared, mutable state.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this interview trap. Structs are great for models, but classes are better when you need shared, mutable state.
